children: By Niket Nishant and Utkarsh    Hathi

Wall Street's main indexes retreated on Tuesday, pausing a two-day rebound in tech shares, after a hotter-than-expected October inflation reading reinforced fears that the Federal Reserve could keep interest rates higher for longer.

Earlier in the day, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise interest rates by at least 25 basis points next month even if inflation cooled in October. If price pressures accelerated, policymakers should consider a half-percentage-point increase, he said.
Traders are pricing in an almost 99% chance of a hike in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
"There are some fears that underlying price pressures are starting to build again. It creates some concern," said James McCann, senior economist at Edward Jones.
"Markets had been pricing out some of the Fed tightening in recent weeks. Now it's probably being forced to contemplate a bit more tightening."
At 09:47 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average
fell 257.10 points, or 0.49%, to 52,132.65, the S&P 500
CBOE:SPX
lost 45.94 points, or 0.61%, to 7,504.00 and the Nasdaq Composite
Among rate-sensitive sectors, financials
rose 0.15%, while utilities
and real estate
were among the laggards.
Nine of 11 major S&P 500 sectors were in negative territory.
NVIDIA, ANTHROPIC TEST AI SENTIMENT
Shares of Nvidia
, the second-most valuable company in the world, slipped 4.4%.

Jensen Huang's affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, alleged to be a spy for Beijing, facilitated the shipment of at least $7.5 billion worth of the company's chips through Chinese firms, The Information reported.
As CEO of the company at the heart of the AI boom, Huang's leadership and future at Nvidia are crucial to investors.
Other chip makers were subdued, with the broader semiconductor index
declining 0.9% after two consecutive sessions of gains, reflecting increasing volatility in the AI trade.

Attention is also turning to Anthropic's (ANT.O) expected public listing later this month. The AI lab revealed that its initial public offering is expected to raise as much as $64.4 billion, giving the company a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.4 trillion.
A listing by Anthropic could also force other AI heavyweights to compete harder for investor dollars.
Neocloud firm CoreWeave
is expected to report quarterly earnings after market close on Tuesday. Questions about the sustainability of the AI boom and the company's debt burden have pressured the stock recently.
Shares of CoreWeave edged 0.8% higher, while those of its peer Nebius
fell 1%.
Media giant Skydance
dropped 9% after it announced cost-cutting plans and warned that the underperformance of Warner Bros' film slate would impact fourth-quarter profit by up to $200 million.
Still, cooling oil prices offered some comfort, with Brent crude futures
slipping below $90 a barrel for the first time since August.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 4.01-to-1 ratio on the NYSE, and by 2.63-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P 500 posted 4 new 52-week highs and 3 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 23 new highs and 84 new lows.
Indexes down: Dow 0.49%, S&P 500 0.61%, Nasdaq 0.74%
